marketplace.name: eric-way
marketplace.description: Eric's agent workflow: skills packaged as installable plugins

plugins.name: global
plugins.description: Eric's always-on working rules: finding the right repository, issue and sub-issue hygiene, open-source conduct, and plan grilling.
plugins.longDescription: Use Eric Global in every session, whatever the project. It covers locating or cloning the right repository before starting, keeping one outcome per GitHub issue and splitting independently deliverable parts, minimizing maintainer disturbance when contributing to projects Eric does not lead, and stress-testing a plan before any code is written.
defaultPrompt: Use $repo to find or clone the right repository before starting.
Use $grill to interrogate this plan before we build it.

plugins.name: project
plugins.description: Cross-language project standards: domain modeling, GitHub Actions hygiene, test judgment, and the pre-commit gate.
plugins.longDescription: Use Eric Project in any repository where Eric writes code. It carries the language-agnostic rules that apply to the project itself: modeling business state, ownership, and side-effect boundaries; keeping GitHub Actions pinned to verified releases and lint-clean; deciding which behavior actually deserves a test; and running the repository's own checks before committing.
defaultPrompt: Use $writing-tests to decide which behavior needs testing.

plugins.name: js
plugins.description: Eric's JavaScript and TypeScript standards plus the pre-commit checklist for JS/TS changes.
plugins.longDescription: Use Eric JS in any JavaScript or TypeScript project. It covers package-manager and tooling defaults, and the pre-commit checklist for formatting, linting, type checking, tests, and unused code.
defaultPrompt: Use $javascript when creating or working in a JS/TS project.
Run $js-checklist before committing these TypeScript changes.

plugins.name: rust
plugins.description: Eric's Rust standards plus the pre-commit checklist for Rust changes.
plugins.longDescription: Use Eric Rust in any Rust project. It covers data shapes, module structure, error handling, validation, and generated contracts, plus the pre-commit checklist for fmt, check, Clippy, tests, and dependency audits.
defaultPrompt: Use $rust when implementing or reviewing Rust code.
Run $rust-checklist before committing these Rust changes.

plugins.name: python
plugins.description: Eric's pre-commit checklist for Python changes.
plugins.longDescription: Use Eric Python in any Python project. It covers the pre-commit checklist for formatting, linting, type checking, tests, and dependency or security audits.
defaultPrompt: Run $python-checklist before committing these Python changes.

plugins.name: frontend
plugins.description: Eric's frontend and React standards for TS/JS UI work, plus browser end-to-end testing.
plugins.longDescription: Use Eric Frontend for TS/JS user interfaces. It covers feature-slice structure, styling boundaries, server-state and interaction-state ownership, React component conventions, and browser end-to-end verification with screenshots and real interaction checks.
defaultPrompt: Use $frontend to implement this UI in Eric's style.
Use $react for this component's hooks and props.

plugins.name: backend
plugins.description: Eric's backend service boundaries and Node.js stack choices.
plugins.longDescription: Use Eric Backend for server-side services. It covers thin transport handlers, service/core ownership, DTO placement, validation boundaries, bootstrap wiring, and the preferred Node.js stack for APIs, databases, migrations, and background jobs.
defaultPrompt: Use $backend to implement or review this service boundary.

plugins.name: desktop
plugins.description: Shared desktop application principles for Electron and Tauri apps.
plugins.longDescription: Use Eric Desktop in any desktop app, Electron or Tauri. It covers local storage and migrations, cross-service and cross-language contracts, treating local service data as server state in the renderer, navigation and external-link handling, and preferring framework or OS primitives.
defaultPrompt: Use $desktop for the shared desktop principles in this app.

plugins.name: tauri
plugins.description: Tauri v2 conventions: command responsiveness, async execution, and generated frontend contracts.
plugins.longDescription: Use Eric Tauri in Tauri v2 apps. It covers choosing Tauri, assessing a command's duration and blocking work before deciding sync or async, moving blocking I/O or CPU work off the async runtime, and generating frontend command contracts.
defaultPrompt: Use $tauri for this Tauri command's responsiveness and contracts.

plugins.name: electron
plugins.description: Electron conventions: browser surfaces, Node integration, and IPC.
plugins.longDescription: Use Eric Electron in Electron apps. It covers when Electron is the right choice over a thin WebView, browser surface ownership, Node integration, and the preferred IPC toolkit.
defaultPrompt: Use $electron for Electron selection, browser surfaces, and IPC.

plugins.name: review
plugins.description: Review code against Eric's standards, prepare GitHub pull requests for review, and produce Guided Review walkthroughs.
plugins.longDescription: Use Eric Review when judging code. It covers concrete findings ordered by severity, implementation degradation and overengineering, GitHub pull request viewed-state mechanics for focusing the changed-files view, and Guided Review artifacts with a reading order, line map, risk focus, and verification focus backed by code evidence.
defaultPrompt: Use $review to review this change against Eric's standards.
Use $guided-review to produce a walkthrough of this pull request.
